why: docs/ai/lcc-r12/m0-gate-a-receipt.json binds its upstream manifest by the path .tmp-new2/m0-upstream/objects.json. That path is excluded by .gitignore:128 (.tmp-new2/), so the manifest could never be at HEAD and a clone could not check the receipt's denominator. NEW2 owns .tmp-new2/ and publishes the identical bytes at a tracked path here. The receipt is LCC-owned and was not edited.

committedEquivalent.provedBy: sha256sum on both paths and cmp, 2026-08-30, NEW2 session df61f64f

whatItIsTheAuthorityFor.note: S3 object listing of the AWS Open Data metadata/parquet prefix at walk time: key, size, etag, lastModified per object. Public data, CC-BY-4.0, Copyright Act s.52(1)(q)(iv). Contains no judgment text.

stillOpen.detail: The receipt still names the scratch path. Whether to amend manifest.path to the committed one is LCC's decision about its own gate artifact, not NEW2's. Until it does, a verifier must follow this file. The bytes are reproducible from HEAD either way.

notClaimed: That this file makes the receipt self-verifying. It makes the bound bytes recoverable from a clone; the receipt's path string is unchanged.
That the manifest was re-walked. It was not. These are the walk-time bytes, copied, not regenerated.
